lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the pulvinus, paired asymmetric flowers, specialized staminodes and hook-style trigger mechanism as the close-family contrast with Cannaceae.

project_scope.note: The current project pool contains Thalia geniculata. Kew accepts the species; FNA documents its U.S. native range mainly in Florida and Louisiana, so local Texas/project-range status remains a separate species-level question.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look at the leaf stalk just below the blade for a pulvinus, then inspect the asymmetric flower. Marantaceae has only one fertile stamen with one theca plus highly specialized sterile staminodes; the style is hook-shaped and participates in an explosive pollen-transfer mechanism.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Rhizomatous perennial herbs with broad leaves, open sheaths and a distinct distal petiole thickening called a pulvinus; blades are often asymmetric around the midrib.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual and asymmetric, commonly in paired cymules. Sepals 3; petals 3, fused at base. Only one stamen is fertile and monothecal; specialized staminodes include a hooded/cucullate member and a firm callose member.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Fleshy or capsular depending on genus; ovary inferior and commonly 1- or 3-locular with one ovule per locule, yielding few seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Pulvinus + one fertile stamen + hooded/callose staminodes + hook-style trigger mechanism points strongly to Marantaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: pulvinus → paired asymmetric flower → one fertile stamen → hooded/callose staminodes → hook-shaped style → few-seeded fruit → Cannaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Marantaceae looks canna-like until you zoom into the pollination machinery. The flower is a mechanical device built from one fertile stamen, specialized staminodes and a spring-loaded style.

steps.title: 1 · Find the pulvinus below the blade
steps.look_for: A thickened jointlike region at the top of the petiole immediately below the blade.
steps.why_it_matters: The pulvinus is a strong vegetative family clue and explains the leaf-movement behavior seen in many Marantaceae.

steps.title: 2 · Look for paired asymmetric flowers
steps.look_for: Flowers occur in small paired units within a branched, bracteate inflorescence; paired flowers may be mirror images.
steps.why_it_matters: This helps distinguish the Marantaceae inflorescence architecture from a simple canna flower cluster.

steps.title: 3 · Find the one fertile stamen
steps.look_for: Only one stamen is fertile, and its anther has one theca; the remaining staminal structures are sterile and modified.
steps.why_it_matters: This links Marantaceae to Cannaceae while setting up the deeper split.

steps.title: 4 · Identify the hooded and callose staminodes
steps.look_for: One inner staminode is hood-shaped/cucullate; another is firm/callose and functions in the trigger mechanism.
steps.why_it_matters: These specialized staminodes are among the strongest family-level differences from Cannaceae.

steps.title: 5 · Follow the hook-shaped style
steps.look_for: A narrow hooked style held by the hooded staminode and released during pollination.
steps.why_it_matters: The style mechanism is one of the most memorable examples of functional floral morphology in the learner.

steps.title: 6 · Compare ovules and seeds with Canna
steps.look_for: Inferior ovary with usually one ovule per locule, producing only 1–3 seeds rather than a many-seeded warty capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the strongest reproductive tie-breaker when flowers are confusing.

comparisons.title: Marantaceae vs Cannaceae
comparisons.rule: Marantaceae: pulvinus; specialized hooded/callose staminodes; hook-shaped style; one ovule per locule; few-seeded fruit. Cannaceae: no comparable trigger-staminode system; flat petaloid style; many ovules per locule; warty many-seeded capsule.

comparisons.title: Marantaceae vs Musaceae
comparisons.rule: Both have large broad leaves, but Marantaceae has a distinct pulvinus and highly specialized one-stamen floral trigger system; bananas have a very different inflorescence and flower structure.

visual_lesson.caveat: Broad canna-like leaves are not enough. Marantaceae is best confirmed from the pulvinus and the specialized flower mechanism.

genera.fast_cue: wetland canna-like herb + distinct pulvinus + spreading/paniclelike inflorescence + specialized Marantaceae flower
